source_user: Advanced cluster case RoCE-24: Diagnose a RoCE-based GPU cluster whose collective communication has unstable tail latency. Variant 24 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: check lossless-priority configuration, PFC/ECN, MTU, route symmetry, congestion, NIC counters, queue pairs, and whether a fallback path is hiding the real fault. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat this as a provisional cluster_tool_use analysis for the stated RoCE variant, focused on diagnostic procedure and safe commands. Assume a multi-node GPU collective workload, but do not assume RoCE is lossless, GPU-direct is active, routes are symmetric, or that no fallback transport is hiding the fault. Separate measured facts, estimates, and unknowns. Inventory GPU/NIC/switch-port topology, PCIe/NVLink affinity, firmware/driver/library versions, MTU, link speed, VLAN and priority mapping, queue-pair count, message-size and concurrency distributions, clock synchronization, and actual transport selection. Trace the path from the collective call through verbs work requests/completions and registered host/GPU buffers to NIC, fabric, and peer; correlate application timestamps with NIC and switch counters rather than treating either as causal proof.

Falsifiable hypothesis: unstable tails are caused by a path/configuration mismatch or congestion event, not by an unmeasured workload change. Under fixed placement, software, warm-up, message mix, concurrency, and sample count, interleave a matched baseline and the suspected configuration. Record latency in ms or µs as distributions (p50/p95/p99 and outliers), collective/step time, throughput, timeout/retry/completion errors, NIC drops and retransmission indicators, switch drops, ECN marks, PFC pause frames/duration, link utilization, queue depth, and GPU utilization. Support the hypothesis only if p95 and p99 improve by at least 10% with confidence intervals and without worsening p99 step time, errors, drops, pauses, ECN, or correctness.

Use a read-only inventory first, then isolate one variable at a time: verify MTU end to end, route symmetry and ECMP, priority/PFC/ECN consistency, congestion and oversubscription, NIC queue-pair and completion behavior, memory registration, and GPU-direct versus host-staging transfers. Confirm the selected transport and detect fallback explicitly. For tool use, capture command versions, timestamps, exit status, and redacted outputs; do not change fabric settings from an unvalidated suggestion. For design, require per-hop configuration invariants, telemetry, capacity headroom, and a canary path. For performance, randomize or interleave runs and report uncertainty and confounders. For troubleshooting, stop at the first failing layer and reproduce with a minimal controlled workload.

Apply changes only in a scoped canary with an abort budget. Roll back immediately on any correctness mismatch, timeout, completion error, link flap, or more than 5% regression in p99 latency, drops, pause duration, or step time; preserve before/after snapshots. Do not claim improvement until synchronized application, verbs, NIC, switch, queue, pause, ECN, error, and link telemetry agrees with the latency result. Unknown platform capabilities and vendor-specific counter meanings remain evidence-required.
risks: RoCE losslessness, topology, GPU-direct behavior, counter semantics, and fallback are platform-dependent and unverified.
Counters may not explain end-to-end tails without synchronized correlation.
A mitigation can worsen pauses, drops, retries, or correctness if applied without a canary.
evidence_required: topology, route, MTU, priority, PFC/ECN, firmware, queue, and transport inventory
interleaved matched baseline with raw percentile distributions and uncertainty by message size and route
synchronized application, verbs, NIC, switch, queue, pause, ECN, error, and link telemetry
correctness checks, scoped canary, rollback thresholds, and redacted command logs
